question.problem:
The graph of the function $y = f(x)$ is given below. Find $a$ and $b$ such that $f(x) \rightarrow a$ as $x \rightarrow \infty$ and $f(x) \rightarrow b$ as $x  \rightarrow -\infty.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194111/assets/77305c6fdeb2b6f3cc0b427924e418938c07caac79843cc6992da799675aad4f.png)
question.worked_solution:
- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ grows larger and larger without bound (as indicated by the arrow). We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x) \rightarrow \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x\rightarrow \infty
$$

Therefore, $a = \infty.$

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $-2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x) \rightarrow -2 \quad \text{as} \quad x\rightarrow -\infty
$$

Therefore, $b = -2.$
